# Summary Statistics for our two Variables

```{r}
summary_stats <- counties_clean %>%
  summarise(counties = n(),
    mean_density = mean(density_per_sqmi),
    median_density = median(density_per_sqmi),
    mean_income = mean(median_household_income_usd),
    median_income = median(median_household_income_usd),
    min_income = min(median_household_income_usd),
    max_income = max(median_household_income_usd))

summary_stats
```

summary_stats
## Research Question

Is there a significant linear relationship between population density and median household income across U.S. counties?

# Set Up and Clean the Dataset 
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, error = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
counties_raw <- read.csv("../data/us-counties-all-data.csv")

head(counties_raw)
names(counties_raw)

counties_clean <- counties_raw %>% 
  select(fips, name, state, density_per_sqmi, median_household_income_usd) %>% 
  drop_na(density_per_sqmi, median_household_income_usd)

head(counties_clean)
glimpse(counties_clean)
nrow(counties_raw) - nrow(counties_clean) # determine how many rows were removed from the drop_na 
```


# Scatterplot between population density and median household income for visualiation

```{r}
ggplot(counties_clean, aes(x = density_per_sqmi, y = median_household_income_usd)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  scale_x_log10() + 
  labs(title = "Population Density vs. Median Household Income", x = "Population Density per Square Mile (log scale)", y = "Median Household Income (USD)") + theme_minimal()

ggplot(counties_clean, aes(x = density_per_sqmi, y = median_household_income_usd)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)  + 
  labs(title = "Population Density vs. Median Household Income", x = "Population Density per Square Mile (linear scale)", y = "Median Household Income (USD)") + theme_minimal()
```

# Compare Difference Between Linear and Logarithmic Model
```{r}
model_linear <- lm(median_household_income_usd ~ density_per_sqmi, data = counties_clean)

model_log <- lm(median_household_income_usd ~ log10(density_per_sqmi), data = counties_clean) # Log Model is better, R² of 0.1419, R approximately 0.377, p-value: < 2.2e-16

summary(model_linear)
summary(model_log)

plot(model_log, which = 1) # ideally, the red line should be approximately horizontal around zero but it's not so it suggests the relationship may not be perfectly linear 
plot(model_log, which = 2) # the Q-Q plot indicates that the residuals deviate from a normal distribution, but sample size large enough and we can still proceed with acknowledging this 
```
# 95% Confidence Interval
```{r}
confint(model_log, level = 0.95)
```
we are 95% confident that, for every tenfold increase in population density, the mean county median household income increases by between 7746 and 9204 USD

# Final Plot that is more Aesthetic
```{r}
final_plot <- ggplot(counties_clean, aes(x = density_per_sqmi, y = median_household_income_usd)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, color = "gray40") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  labs(title = "Population Density and Household Income",
    subtitle = "U.S. Counties | Logarithmic Population Density",
    x = "Population Density (People per Square Mile, Log Scale)",
    y = "Median Household Income (USD)",
    caption = "Source: County Maps US / U.S. Census Bureau") +
  theme_minimal()

final_plot
```

# important regression statistics for statistical analysis?
```{r}
model_summary <- summary(model_log)

regression_results <- tibble(
  Statistic = c("Sample Size",
    "Intercept",
    "Slope",
    "R-squared",
    "Adjusted R-squared",
    "P-value for slope",
    "Residual Standard Error"),
  Value = c(nobs(model_log),
    coef(model_log)[1],
    coef(model_log)[2],
    model_summary$r.squared,
    model_summary$adj.r.squared,
    coef(model_summary)[2, 4],
    model_summary$sigma))

knitr::kable(regression_results, digits = 4)
```
## Hypothesis Testing

We are testing whether there is a significant linear
relationship between log-transformed population density
and median household income across U.S. counties.

Null Hypothesis: H0: β1 = 0

Alternative Hypothesis: HA: β1 ≠ 0

Significance Level: α = 0.05
```{r}
summary(model_log)
```
Because the p-value of 2.2e-16 is less than 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis.

This provides statistically significant evidence of a positive relationship between log-transformed population density and median household income
